definitions.explanation: Describes someone who is honest and sincere to the point of seeming naive or unsophisticated. Often implies a positive quality of earnest dedication without guile, though the character {愚|ぐ} (foolish) adds a note of self-deprecation.

examples.japanese: {愚直|ぐちょく}に{働|はたら}く
{彼|かれ}は{愚直|ぐちょく}なまでに{正直|しょうじき}だ。
examples.english: He is honest to the point of being simple-minded.

examples.japanese: {愚直|ぐちょく}に{一|ひと}つのことを{続|つづ}けてきた{職人|しょくにん}の{姿|すがた}に{感動|かんどう}した。
examples.english: I was moved by the craftsman who had earnestly dedicated himself to one thing.

notes:
ADJECTIVE TYPE: Na-adjective. Uses な before nouns: {愚直|ぐちょく}な{性格|せいかく}.

ADVERBIAL FORM: {愚直|ぐちょく}に (with honest simplicity)

NUANCE: Despite containing {愚|ぐ} (foolish), {愚直|ぐちょく} is often used positively to describe admirable dedication and sincerity. It's frequently used self-deprecatingly or to praise someone's earnest effort.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {愚直|ぐちょく}に{働|はたら}く (to work earnestly)
- {愚直|ぐちょく}に{続|つづ}ける (to continue steadfastly)
- {愚直|ぐちょく}なまでに (to the point of being simplistic)

RELATED WORDS:
- {実直|じっちょく} (honest, sincere - more neutral)
- {朴訥|ぼくとつ} (simple, artless)
- {馬鹿正直|ばかしょうじき} (foolishly honest)
